entries.name: The Lord's Prayer
entries.epithet: Our Father which art in heaven
entries.occasion: A pattern for his disciples' prayers

lines: After this manner therefore pray ye: Our Father which art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name.
Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done in earth, as it is in heaven.
Give us this day our daily bread.
And forgive us our debts, as we forgive our debtors.
And lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil: For thine is the kingdom, and the power, and the glory, for ever. Amen.

entries.summary: The prayer Jesus gave his disciples as a pattern: God's name, kingdom and will first, then our bread, our forgiveness and our protection.
entries.story: In the Sermon on the Mount Jesus told his hearers not to pray like the hypocrites, to be seen, nor to pray with 'vain repetitions, as the heathen do.' Then: 'After this manner therefore pray ye: Our Father which art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name.' Luke records that on another occasion a disciple asked, 'Lord, teach us to pray', and Jesus gave the same prayer. (The closing words, 'For thine is the kingdom, and the power, and the glory, for ever', are not in the oldest manuscripts of Matthew; the King James Version keeps them.)
entries.meaning: The prayer puts God first: his name, his kingdom, his will. Only then does it ask for daily needs, forgiveness and protection. It says 'our', not 'my', and it ties our being forgiven to our forgiving others (Matthew 6:14-15).
entries.daily: The Lord's Prayer fits any day, prayed as it stands or used as an outline to fill with your own words. 'Give us this day our daily bread' asks for today's needs, not a lifetime's supply, so it is a prayer to pray again tomorrow.
entries.pray_it: Father, may your name be honoured in my life today. Give me what I need for this day, forgive me as I forgive others, and keep me from evil.

key_verses.text: For if ye forgive men their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you:

entries.name: Prayer in secret
entries.epithet: Enter into thy closet
entries.occasion: Teaching against praying to be seen

lines: But thou, when thou prayest, enter into thy closet, and when thou hast shut thy door, pray to thy Father which is in secret; and thy Father which seeth in secret shall reward thee openly.

entries.summary: Jesus warned against praying to be seen, and told his hearers to pray to their Father in secret.
entries.story: Some prayed standing in the synagogues and on street corners, 'that they may be seen of men.' Jesus said, 'They have their reward.' Instead: 'enter into thy closet, and when thou hast shut thy door, pray to thy Father which is in secret.' There is no need for many words, 'for your Father knoweth what things ye have need of, before ye ask him.'
entries.meaning: Prayer is not a performance. God is not impressed by length or eloquence; he is a Father who already knows what we need, and wants us to come to him anyway.
entries.daily: Find a place and a time where no one is watching: a room, a walk, the first minutes of the morning. Shut the door on distractions, and speak to God simply.
entries.pray_it: Father, you see me here where no one else does. You know what I need before I say it. I come to you just as I am.

key_verses.text: Be not ye therefore like unto them: for your Father knoweth what things ye have need of, before ye ask him.

entries.name: Ask, seek, knock
entries.epithet: Ask, and it shall be given you
entries.occasion: After teaching the Lord's Prayer

lines: And I say unto you, Ask, and it shall be given you; seek, and ye shall find; knock, and it shall be opened unto you.
For every one that asketh receiveth; and he that seeketh findeth; and to him that knocketh it shall be opened.

entries.summary: Through the story of a friend at midnight, Jesus taught persistence in prayer, and promised that the Father gives the Holy Spirit to those who ask.
entries.story: Jesus told of a man who knocked on a friend's door at midnight to borrow three loaves. The friend called out, 'Trouble me not', but got up and gave him what he needed 'because of his importunity', his shameless persistence. 'Ask, and it shall be given you; seek, and ye shall find; knock, and it shall be opened unto you.' If earthly fathers give good gifts, 'how much more shall your heavenly Father give the Holy Spirit to them that ask him?'
entries.meaning: God is not a reluctant neighbour; the point of the story is 'how much more'. Persistence in prayer is not wearing God down, but staying close to him and continuing to trust.
entries.daily: Keep asking. Bring the same need back tomorrow, and the day after. Ask especially for the Holy Spirit, the gift Jesus promised the Father would give.
entries.pray_it: Father, I keep knocking because I trust you. Give me what is good, and above all fill me with your Holy Spirit.

key_verses.text: If ye then, being evil, know how to give good gifts unto your children: how much more shall your heavenly Father give the Holy Spirit to them that ask him?

entries.name: The widow who would not give up
entries.epithet: Men ought always to pray, and not to faint
entries.occasion: A parable about praying without losing heart

lines: And he spake a parable unto them to this end, that men ought always to pray, and not to faint;

entries.summary: A parable of a widow who kept asking an unjust judge for justice until he gave in, told so that we would always pray and not lose heart.
entries.story: Luke says plainly why Jesus told it: 'that men ought always to pray, and not to faint.' A judge who feared neither God nor man was pestered by a widow asking for justice. At last he said he would help her, 'lest by her continual coming she weary me.' Jesus said, 'shall not God avenge his own elect, which cry day and night unto him?' Then he asked, 'when the Son of man cometh, shall he find faith on the earth?'
entries.meaning: Again the point is contrast: if an unjust judge gives in, how much more will a loving God hear his children. Faith shows itself by not giving up.
entries.daily: When an answer is slow in coming, keep praying rather than letting discouragement win. Praying day and night is the opposite of fainting.
entries.pray_it: Lord, when your answer seems slow, keep me from losing heart. I will keep bringing this to you, because I trust that you hear.

key_verses.text: And shall not God avenge his own elect, which cry day and night unto him, though he bear long with them?

entries.name: The Pharisee and the tax collector
entries.epithet: God be merciful to me a sinner
entries.occasion: A parable for those who trusted in their own righteousness

lines: And the publican, standing afar off, would not lift up so much as his eyes unto heaven, but smote upon his breast, saying, God be merciful to me a sinner.

entries.summary: Two men went up to the temple to pray: a Pharisee who thanked God he was not like others, and a tax collector who could only ask for mercy. The second went home justified.
entries.story: Jesus told this parable 'unto certain which trusted in themselves that they were righteous, and despised others.' The Pharisee stood and prayed 'with himself', listing his fasting and tithing and thanking God he was not like 'this publican.' The tax collector stood far off, would not even lift his eyes to heaven, beat his breast and said, 'God be merciful to me a sinner.' Jesus said, 'this man went down to his house justified rather than the other.'
entries.meaning: God hears humility, not self-promotion: 'every one that exalteth himself shall be abased; and he that humbleth himself shall be exalted' (Luke 18:14).
entries.daily: Before you pray, drop your comparisons with other people. The shortest prayer in this story was the one God accepted, and it can be prayed anywhere, at any moment.
entries.pray_it: God, be merciful to me, a sinner. I have nothing to boast of; I come only asking for your mercy.

key_verses.text: I tell you, this man went down to his house justified rather than the other: for every one that exalteth himself shall be abased; and he that humbleth himself shall be exalted.

entries.name: Pray for your enemies
entries.epithet: Pray for them which despitefully use you
entries.occasion: Teaching on love for enemies

lines: But I say unto you, Love your enemies, bless them that curse you, do good to them that hate you, and pray for them which despitefully use you, and persecute you;

entries.summary: Jesus told his followers to love their enemies and to pray for those who persecute them, because their Father in heaven is kind to all.
entries.story: People had heard it said, 'Thou shalt love thy neighbour, and hate thine enemy.' Jesus said, 'Love your enemies, bless them that curse you, do good to them that hate you, and pray for them which despitefully use you, and persecute you.' The reason is the Father's own character: 'he maketh his sun to rise on the evil and on the good.'
entries.meaning: Jesus did it himself on the cross (Luke 23:34), and Stephen did the same as he died (Acts 7:60). Praying for an enemy changes the one who prays.
entries.daily: Name someone who has hurt you, and pray for their good, not only for your protection from them. It may be the hardest prayer of the day.
entries.pray_it: Father, I bring you the person who has hurt me. Bless them, do them good, and change my heart toward them, as you are kind to all.

key_verses.text: That ye may be the children of your Father which is in heaven: for he maketh his sun to rise on the evil and on the good, and sendeth rain on the just and on the unjust.

entries.name: Where two or three are gathered
entries.epithet: There am I in the midst of them
entries.occasion: Teaching his disciples about life together

lines: Again I say unto you, That if two of you shall agree on earth as touching any thing that they shall ask, it shall be done for them of my Father which is in heaven.
For where two or three are gathered together in my name, there am I in the midst of them.

entries.summary: Jesus promised that when two agree in prayer, and two or three gather in his name, he is with them.
entries.story: Speaking to his disciples about life together, Jesus said, 'if two of you shall agree on earth as touching any thing that they shall ask, it shall be done for them of my Father which is in heaven. For where two or three are gathered together in my name, there am I in the midst of them.'
entries.meaning: Prayer is not only private. The first believers 'continued stedfastly' in prayers together (Acts 2:42), and Jesus promised his presence to even the smallest gathering.
entries.daily: Pray with someone: a husband or wife, a friend, a child, a colleague, even for two minutes. Agreeing together in prayer is one of the promises Jesus attached to it.
entries.pray_it: Lord Jesus, you are here with us as we pray together. Hear what we agree to ask in your name.

key_verses.text: For where two or three are gathered together in my name, there am I in the midst of them.

entries.name: The Lord of the harvest
entries.epithet: Pray ye therefore the Lord of the harvest
entries.occasion: Seeing the crowds like sheep without a shepherd

lines: Then saith he unto his disciples, The harvest truly is plenteous, but the labourers are few;
Pray ye therefore the Lord of the harvest, that he will send forth labourers into his harvest.

entries.summary: Moved with compassion for the crowds, Jesus told his disciples to pray that God would send workers out into his harvest.
entries.story: Jesus saw the multitudes scattered 'as sheep having no shepherd', and was moved with compassion. He said, 'The harvest truly is plenteous, but the labourers are few; Pray ye therefore the Lord of the harvest, that he will send forth labourers into his harvest.' In the very next chapter he sent out the twelve.
entries.meaning: Compassion leads to prayer, and prayer leads to action: the disciples who were told to pray for workers became the workers.
entries.daily: When you see a need you cannot meet, pray for God to send the right people, and be ready to be one of them.
entries.pray_it: Lord of the harvest, the need around me is great. Send people to help, to care and to share the good news, and send me.

key_verses.text: But when he saw the multitudes, he was moved with compassion on them, because they fainted, and were scattered abroad, as sheep having no shepherd.

entries.name: Before dawn
entries.epithet: A great while before day
entries.occasion: The morning after a day of healing
entries.summary: After a long day of healing, Jesus rose before dawn and went to a solitary place to pray.
entries.story: The evening before, the whole city had gathered at the door, and Jesus had healed many. 'And in the morning, rising up a great while before day, he went out, and departed into a solitary place, and there prayed.' Simon and the others hunted for him: 'All men seek for thee.' Jesus answered that they must go on to the next towns.
entries.meaning: Even at the height of his popularity Jesus made time alone with his Father, and it was there that his direction became clear. Luke says he often withdrew into the wilderness to pray (Luke 5:16).
entries.daily: Begin before the day begins. A few quiet minutes with God before messages and demands arrive can set the course of everything else.
entries.pray_it: Father, before the day's demands begin, I come to you. Show me what matters today, and what I can leave with you.

key_verses.text: And in the morning, rising up a great while before day, he went out, and departed into a solitary place, and there prayed.
And he withdrew himself into the wilderness, and prayed.

entries.name: All night before choosing the twelve
entries.epithet: He continued all night in prayer to God
entries.occasion: Before choosing his apostles
entries.summary: Before choosing his twelve apostles, Jesus went up a mountain and prayed all night.
entries.story: 'And it came to pass in those days, that he went out into a mountain to pray, and continued all night in prayer to God. And when it was day, he called unto him his disciples: and of them he chose twelve, whom also he named apostles.'
entries.meaning: Jesus prayed before his great decisions. Luke shows him praying at his baptism (Luke 3:21), before choosing the twelve, at the transfiguration (Luke 9:29) and in Gethsemane.
entries.daily: Before a big decision, spend unhurried time in prayer first, not just a quick request after the choice has already been made.
entries.pray_it: Lord, I have a decision to make. Before I choose, I bring it to you. Guide my choice, and give me peace about it.

key_verses.text: And it came to pass in those days, that he went out into a mountain to pray, and continued all night in prayer to God.

entries.name: I thank thee, O Father
entries.epithet: Revealed unto babes
entries.occasion: After some towns refused to repent

lines: At that time Jesus answered and said, I thank thee, O Father, Lord of heaven and earth, because thou hast hid these things from the wise and prudent, and hast revealed them unto babes.
Even so, Father: for so it seemed good in thy sight.

entries.summary: Jesus thanked his Father for showing the truth to ordinary people, and then invited everyone who is weary to come to him for rest.
entries.story: After some towns refused to repent, Jesus prayed aloud: 'I thank thee, O Father, Lord of heaven and earth, because thou hast hid these things from the wise and prudent, and hast revealed them unto babes.' Then he turned to the crowd: 'Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest.'
entries.meaning: Thanksgiving was part of Jesus' own praying, even in disappointment, and his thanks for God's way led straight into an invitation.
entries.daily: Thank God for what he has shown you, even on a day when things have not gone your way.
entries.pray_it: Father, thank you for showing yourself to ordinary people like me. I come to you tired, and I receive your rest.

key_verses.text: Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest.

entries.name: At the tomb of Lazarus
entries.epithet: Father, I thank thee that thou hast heard me
entries.occasion: Just before he raised Lazarus

lines: Then they took away the stone from the place where the dead was laid. And Jesus lifted up his eyes, and said, Father, I thank thee that thou hast heard me.
And I knew that thou hearest me always: but because of the people which stand by I said it, that they may believe that thou hast sent me.

entries.summary: Before raising Lazarus, Jesus looked up and thanked his Father for hearing him, so that the people standing by would believe.
entries.story: When the stone was taken away, 'Jesus lifted up his eyes, and said, Father, I thank thee that thou hast heard me. And I knew that thou hearest me always: but because of the people which stand by I said it, that they may believe that thou hast sent me.' Then he cried with a loud voice, 'Lazarus, come forth.'
entries.meaning: Jesus gave thanks before the answer could be seen. His prayer was confident because he knew his Father heard him always.
entries.daily: Thank God ahead of time for hearing you. It is not presumption, but trust.
entries.pray_it: Father, thank you that you hear me. Even before I see the answer, I trust that you are at work.

entries.name: The prayer for his followers
entries.epithet: That they all may be one
entries.occasion: The night before the crucifixion

lines: These words spake Jesus, and lifted up his eyes to heaven, and said, Father, the hour is come; glorify thy Son, that thy Son also may glorify thee:
Neither pray I for these alone, but for them also which shall believe on me through their word;
That they all may be one; as thou, Father, art in me, and I in thee, that they also may be one in us: that the world may believe that thou hast sent me.

entries.summary: On the night before he died, Jesus prayed for himself, for his disciples, and for everyone who would believe through them.
entries.story: After the Last Supper Jesus 'lifted up his eyes to heaven, and said, Father, the hour is come; glorify thy Son, that thy Son also may glorify thee.' He prayed for the disciples he was leaving in the world, that God would 'keep them from the evil.' Then his prayer reached past them to us: 'Neither pray I for these alone, but for them also which shall believe on me through their word; That they all may be one.'
entries.meaning: Jesus prayed for people who did not yet exist: every believer to come. The unity of his people was on his heart the night before the cross.
entries.daily: Pray for the church, including believers you disagree with, that they may be one. And remember that Jesus has prayed for you.
entries.pray_it: Lord Jesus, you prayed for me before I was born. Make your people one, keep us from evil, and let the world believe.

key_verses.text: I pray not that thou shouldest take them out of the world, but that thou shouldest keep them from the evil.

entries.name: Gethsemane
entries.epithet: Not as I will, but as thou wilt
entries.occasion: The night of his arrest

lines: And he went a little farther, and fell on his face, and prayed, saying, O my Father, if it be possible, let this cup pass from me: nevertheless not as I will, but as thou wilt.

entries.summary: In the garden before his arrest, deeply distressed, Jesus asked his Father to take the cup from him, and then yielded to his Father's will.
entries.story: Jesus took Peter, James and John with him and said, 'My soul is exceeding sorrowful, even unto death.' He went a little further, fell on his face and prayed, 'O my Father, if it be possible, let this cup pass from me: nevertheless not as I will, but as thou wilt.' Three times he prayed, and three times he found the disciples asleep: 'Watch and pray, that ye enter not into temptation.' Luke adds that his sweat was 'as it were great drops of blood'.
entries.meaning: Honest prayer can ask for the hard thing to be taken away, and still end in trust: 'thy will be done' (Matthew 26:42).
entries.daily: Tell God honestly what you want, and then hand the outcome to him. Surrender does not mean pretending you have no wishes.
entries.pray_it: Father, this is what I want, and you know it. Yet not my will, but yours be done.

key_verses.text: Watch and pray, that ye enter not into temptation: the spirit indeed is willing, but the flesh is weak.
He went away again the second time, and prayed, saying, O my Father, if this cup may not pass away from me, except I drink it, thy will be done.

entries.name: Father, forgive them
entries.epithet: For they know not what they do
entries.occasion: As he was being crucified

lines: Then said Jesus, Father, forgive them; for they know not what they do. And they parted his raiment, and cast lots.

entries.summary: While he was being crucified, Jesus prayed for the forgiveness of those who put him on the cross.
entries.story: At the place called Calvary they crucified him between two criminals. 'Then said Jesus, Father, forgive them; for they know not what they do.' Below him, the soldiers were dividing his clothes. (Some early manuscripts of Luke do not have this prayer; the King James Version keeps it.)
entries.meaning: Jesus did on the cross what he had taught on the mountain: he prayed for his enemies. Isaiah had said the servant would make 'intercession for the transgressors' (Isaiah 53:12).
entries.daily: Forgiveness often begins as a prayer before it becomes a feeling. Pray for the people who wronged you, even if they never know it.
entries.pray_it: Father, forgive those who have hurt me; they do not fully know what they have done. And forgive me, as I forgive them.

entries.name: Into thy hands
entries.epithet: Father, into thy hands I commend my spirit
entries.occasion: His last words on the cross

lines: And when Jesus had cried with a loud voice, he said, Father, into thy hands I commend my spirit: and having said thus, he gave up the ghost.

entries.summary: Jesus' last words on the cross were a prayer from the Psalms, entrusting himself to his Father.
entries.story: Darkness covered the land from the sixth hour to the ninth, and the veil of the temple was torn. 'And when Jesus had cried with a loud voice, he said, Father, into thy hands I commend my spirit: and having said thus, he gave up the ghost.' His words come from Psalm 31, a prayer of trust: 'Into thine hand I commit my spirit' (Psalm 31:5).
entries.meaning: Jesus died praying. He added one word to the psalm, 'Father', and made the moment of death an act of trust. Stephen prayed the same way as he died (Acts 7:59).
entries.daily: End the day, and every hard moment, by committing yourself into God's hands. Psalm 31:5 is a prayer for bedtime as well as for the end of life.
entries.pray_it: Father, into your hands I commit my spirit, my worries and this night. Keep me.

key_verses.text: Into thine hand I commit my spirit: thou hast redeemed me, O LORD God of truth.

entries.name: Abraham pleads for Sodom
entries.epithet: Shall not the Judge of all the earth do right?
entries.occasion: When God told him Sodom would be destroyed

lines: That be far from thee to do after this manner, to slay the righteous with the wicked: and that the righteous should be as the wicked, that be far from thee: Shall not the Judge of all the earth do right?

entries.summary: Abraham stood before the LORD and asked him to spare Sodom for fifty righteous people, then forty-five, forty, thirty, twenty, and finally ten.
entries.story: When the LORD told Abraham what he meant to do to Sodom, 'Abraham drew near, and said, Wilt thou also destroy the righteous with the wicked?' He appealed to God's own justice: 'Shall not the Judge of all the earth do right?' He asked for fifty righteous, then forty-five, forty, thirty, twenty and ten, and each time God agreed. Abraham knew he was 'but dust and ashes', yet he kept asking.
entries.meaning: This is the Bible's first great prayer for others: bold and humble at once, appealing to God's character. The city was not spared, but 'God remembered Abraham, and sent Lot out' (Genesis 19:29).
entries.daily: Pray for places and people facing trouble or judgement: your town, your country, someone in danger. Praying for others is standing before God on their behalf.
entries.pray_it: Lord, you are the Judge of all the earth, and you do what is right. I ask your mercy for my town and the people in it.

key_verses.text: And Abraham answered and said, Behold now, I have taken upon me to speak unto the Lord, which am but dust and ashes:
And it came to pass, when God destroyed the cities of the plain, that God remembered Abraham, and sent Lot out of the midst of the overthrow, when he overthrew the cities in the which Lot dwelt.

entries.name: The servant's prayer at the well
entries.epithet: Send me good speed this day
entries.occasion: Sent to find a wife for Isaac

lines: And he said, O LORD God of my master Abraham, I pray thee, send me good speed this day, and shew kindness unto my master Abraham.

entries.summary: Sent to find a wife for Isaac, Abraham's servant asked God for a particular sign, and before he had finished praying, Rebekah came to the well.
entries.story: Abraham's servant arrived at a well in Mesopotamia at evening with ten camels. He prayed, 'O LORD God of my master Abraham, I pray thee, send me good speed this day', and asked that the young woman who offered water to him and to his camels would be the one. 'And it came to pass, before he had done speaking, that, behold, Rebekah came out.' When it happened just so, he bowed his head and worshipped the LORD.
entries.meaning: A practical prayer about an ordinary task, answered in an ordinary way, and the servant stopped at once to give thanks.
entries.daily: Pray about the practical tasks of today: a meeting, a journey, a choice. Ask God to go before you, watch for his answer, and thank him when you see it.
entries.pray_it: Lord, go with me in today's tasks and help me do them well. Help me notice your hand, and thank you when I see it.

entries.name: Jacob's prayer before meeting Esau
entries.epithet: I am not worthy of the least of all the mercies
entries.occasion: Afraid of meeting the brother he had cheated
entries.where: On the way home to Canaan

lines: I am not worthy of the least of all the mercies, and of all the truth, which thou hast shewed unto thy servant; for with my staff I passed over this Jordan; and now I am become two bands.
Deliver me, I pray thee, from the hand of my brother, from the hand of Esau: for I fear him, lest he will come and smite me, and the mother with the children.

entries.summary: Afraid of meeting the brother he had cheated, Jacob prayed honestly, confessing his unworthiness and his fear, and holding God to his promise.
entries.story: Twenty years after stealing Esau's blessing, Jacob heard that Esau was coming to meet him with four hundred men. He 'was greatly afraid and distressed.' He prayed, reminding God that he had told him to go home, confessing, 'I am not worthy of the least of all the mercies', and asking, 'Deliver me, I pray thee, from the hand of my brother.' That night he wrestled with God at Peniel. The next day Esau ran to meet him, and embraced him.
entries.meaning: Jacob's prayer has the shape of many good prayers: God's promise, honest confession, a plain request. Fear brought him to prayer instead of driving him away from it.
entries.daily: When you are afraid, say so to God, remind yourself of his promises, and ask plainly for help.
entries.pray_it: Lord, I am not worthy of all your kindness to me. I am afraid of what lies ahead. Rescue me, as you have promised to be with me.

entries.name: Moses stands in the gap
entries.epithet: Blot me, I pray thee, out of thy book
entries.occasion: After Israel made the golden calf

lines: And Moses besought the LORD his God, and said, LORD, why doth thy wrath wax hot against thy people, which thou hast brought forth out of the land of Egypt with great power, and with a mighty hand?

entries.summary: After Israel made the golden calf, Moses pleaded with God for the people, even offering to be blotted out of God's book in their place.
entries.story: While Moses was on the mountain, the people made a golden calf, and God said he would consume them. 'And Moses besought the LORD his God', reminding him of his promises to Abraham, Isaac and Israel, 'And the LORD repented of the evil which he thought to do unto his people.' The next day Moses went up again: 'Oh, this people have sinned a great sin', and if God would not forgive them, 'blot me, I pray thee, out of thy book which thou hast written.'
entries.meaning: Moses is the great intercessor of the Old Testament, willing to stand between God's judgement and the people (Psalm 106:23). He points ahead to Christ, who 'ever liveth to make intercession' for us (Hebrews 7:25).
entries.daily: Stand in the gap for people who have gone wrong, instead of only criticising them. Pray for them by name.
entries.pray_it: Lord, I bring before you people who have turned away from you. Remember your promises, and have mercy on them.

key_verses.text: And the LORD repented of the evil which he thought to do unto his people.
Wherefore he is able also to save them to the uttermost that come unto God by him, seeing he ever liveth to make intercession for them.

entries.name: Show me thy glory
entries.epithet: If thy presence go not with me, carry us not up hence
entries.occasion: After the golden calf, before leaving Sinai
entries.where: The tent of meeting and Mount Sinai

lines: And he said unto him, If thy presence go not with me, carry us not up hence.
And he said, I beseech thee, shew me thy glory.

entries.summary: Moses refused to go on without God's presence, and asked to see his glory; God passed by and proclaimed his name.
entries.story: After the golden calf, God said he would send an angel ahead of the people but would not go among them himself. Moses answered, 'If thy presence go not with me, carry us not up hence.' God agreed. Then Moses asked for more: 'I beseech thee, shew me thy glory.' God put him in a cleft of the rock and passed by, proclaiming, 'The LORD, The LORD God, merciful and gracious, longsuffering, and abundant in goodness and truth.'
entries.meaning: The deepest request in prayer is for God himself, his presence and his glory, more than any of his gifts. God answered by showing his character: mercy and grace.
entries.daily: Before asking God to bless your plans, ask him to go with you. His presence matters more than success.
entries.pray_it: Lord, I do not want to go anywhere today without you. Go with me, and show me more of who you are.

key_verses.text: And the LORD passed by before him, and proclaimed, The LORD, The LORD God, merciful and gracious, longsuffering, and abundant in goodness and truth,

entries.name: The priestly blessing
entries.epithet: The LORD bless thee, and keep thee
entries.occasion: A blessing to speak over Israel

lines: The LORD bless thee, and keep thee:
The LORD make his face shine upon thee, and be gracious unto thee:
The LORD lift up his countenance upon thee, and give thee peace.

entries.summary: The blessing God gave Aaron and his sons to speak over Israel, putting God's name on his people.
entries.story: God told Moses to tell Aaron and his sons, 'On this wise ye shall bless the children of Israel.' The blessing has three lines, each one naming the LORD. God added, 'they shall put my name upon the children of Israel; and I will bless them.'
entries.meaning: This is a prayer spoken over other people. It asks for God's protection, his favour and his peace, and it has been spoken over worshippers for thousands of years.
entries.daily: Speak this blessing over your children, your family or a friend, at bedtime or when you part. It is a prayer anyone can pray for someone else.
entries.pray_it: The LORD bless you and keep you. The LORD make his face shine on you and be gracious to you. The LORD look on you with favour, and give you peace.

key_verses.text: And they shall put my name upon the children of Israel; and I will bless them.

entries.name: Hannah's prayer
entries.epithet: Poured out my soul before the LORD
entries.occasion: Longing for a child
entries.where: The house of the LORD at Shiloh

lines: And she vowed a vow, and said, O LORD of hosts, if thou wilt indeed look on the affliction of thine handmaid, and remember me, and not forget thine handmaid, but wilt give unto thine handmaid a man child, then I will give him unto the LORD all the days of his life, and there shall no razor come upon his head.

entries.summary: In bitterness of soul Hannah prayed silently at Shiloh for a son, and vowed to give him back to the LORD.
entries.story: Hannah 'was in bitterness of soul, and prayed unto the LORD, and wept sore.' Her lips moved but her voice was not heard, and Eli the priest thought she was drunk. She told him she was not drunk, but 'have poured out my soul before the LORD.' Eli blessed her, and 'her countenance was no more sad', before she knew the answer. In time she bore Samuel.
entries.meaning: Hannah's prayer is honest grief brought to God, and her peace came from having prayed, before anything had changed.
entries.daily: Pour out your heart to God, silently if you need to. You do not need polished words, only honest ones.
entries.pray_it: Lord, you see my sorrow. I pour out my heart to you. I leave this with you, and I ask for your peace.

key_verses.text: And Hannah answered and said, No, my lord, I am a woman of a sorrowful spirit: I have drunken neither wine nor strong drink, but have poured out my soul before the LORD.
For this child I prayed; and the LORD hath given me my petition which I asked of him:

entries.name: David's prayer of wonder
entries.epithet: Who am I, O Lord GOD?
entries.occasion: After God promised him an everlasting house

lines: Then went king David in, and sat before the LORD, and he said, Who am I, O Lord GOD? and what is my house, that thou hast brought me hitherto?
Wherefore thou art great, O LORD God: for there is none like thee, neither is there any God beside thee, according to all that we have heard with our ears.

entries.summary: After God promised him an everlasting house, David sat before the LORD, overwhelmed, and prayed in wonder and thanks.
entries.story: Through Nathan, God promised David that his throne would be established for ever. 'Then went king David in, and sat before the LORD, and he said, Who am I, O Lord GOD? and what is my house, that thou hast brought me hitherto?' He praised God's greatness, 'for there is none like thee', and asked God to do as he had said.
entries.meaning: David's first response to God's promise was not a list of requests but wonder. Good prayers of thanks often begin with 'Who am I?'
entries.daily: Sit before God and look back: how has he brought you this far? Thank him before you ask him for more.
entries.pray_it: Lord God, who am I that you have brought me this far? There is no one like you. Do as you have promised.

entries.name: Solomon asks for wisdom
entries.epithet: Give therefore thy servant an understanding heart
entries.occasion: When God said, Ask what I shall give thee

lines: Give therefore thy servant an understanding heart to judge thy people, that I may discern between good and bad: for who is able to judge this thy so great a people?

entries.summary: When God invited Solomon to ask for anything, he asked for an understanding heart to lead God's people well, and God gave him wisdom and much more.
entries.story: At Gibeon God appeared to Solomon in a dream: 'Ask what I shall give thee.' Solomon said, 'I am but a little child: I know not how to go out or come in.' He asked for 'an understanding heart to judge thy people, that I may discern between good and bad.' 'And the speech pleased the Lord.' God gave him wisdom, and riches and honour as well.
entries.meaning: Solomon asked for what he needed to serve others well. James makes the same offer to every believer: 'If any of you lack wisdom, let him ask of God' (James 1:5).
entries.daily: Ask God for wisdom for the responsibilities you carry today, at home, at work, and with the people who depend on you.
entries.pray_it: Lord, I often do not know what to do. Give me an understanding heart, so that I can serve the people in my care well.

key_verses.text: If any of you lack wisdom, let him ask of God, that giveth to all men liberally, and upbraideth not; and it shall be given him.

entries.name: Solomon's prayer at the temple
entries.epithet: The heaven of heavens cannot contain thee
entries.occasion: The dedication of the temple

lines: But will God indeed dwell on the earth? behold, the heaven and heaven of heavens cannot contain thee; how much less this house that I have builded?
Yet have thou respect unto the prayer of thy servant, and to his supplication, O LORD my God, to hearken unto the cry and to the prayer, which thy servant prayeth before thee to day:

entries.summary: At the dedication of the temple, Solomon spread out his hands to heaven and asked God to hear every prayer made toward that place, even a foreigner's.
entries.story: Solomon stood before the altar 'and spread forth his hands toward heaven.' He confessed that no building could hold God: 'the heaven and heaven of heavens cannot contain thee; how much less this house that I have builded?' Yet he asked God to hear from heaven whenever his people prayed toward it, in drought, famine, war, captivity and sin, and whenever a stranger came from a far country to pray, 'that all people of the earth may know thy name'.
entries.meaning: Solomon's prayer shows that God's house was meant to be 'an house of prayer for all people' (Isaiah 56:7). God answered by filling the temple with his glory.
entries.daily: Wherever you are, you can turn toward God. Pray about the troubles Solomon named, in your own life and in the world's.
entries.pray_it: Lord, not even the heavens can contain you, yet you hear me. Hear my prayer today, and hear the prayers of people everywhere who call on you.

key_verses.text: Even them will I bring to my holy mountain, and make them joyful in my house of prayer: their burnt offerings and their sacrifices shall be accepted upon mine altar; for mine house shall be called an house of prayer for all people.

entries.name: Elijah on Mount Carmel
entries.epithet: Hear me, O LORD, hear me
entries.occasion: The contest with the prophets of Baal

lines: And it came to pass at the time of the offering of the evening sacrifice, that Elijah the prophet came near, and said, LORD God of Abraham, Isaac, and of Israel, let it be known this day that thou art God in Israel, and that I am thy servant, and that I have done all these things at thy word.
Hear me, O LORD, hear me, that this people may know that thou art the LORD God, and that thou hast turned their heart back again.

entries.summary: After the prophets of Baal had cried out all day with no answer, Elijah prayed a short, simple prayer, and fire fell from heaven.
entries.story: From morning to evening the prophets of Baal shouted, danced and cut themselves, 'that there was neither voice, nor any to answer'. At the time of the evening sacrifice Elijah came near and prayed briefly: 'Hear me, O LORD, hear me, that this people may know that thou art the LORD God, and that thou hast turned their heart back again.' Then the fire of the LORD fell.
entries.meaning: Elijah's prayer was short, and it sought God's glory, not his own. James holds him up as an example: 'The effectual fervent prayer of a righteous man availeth much' (James 5:16).
entries.daily: A long prayer is not a better prayer. Ask God to show himself, for the sake of the people around you.
entries.pray_it: Lord, hear me. Show that you are God, here and today, and turn hearts back to you.

key_verses.text: Confess your faults one to another, and pray one for another, that ye may be healed. The effectual fervent prayer of a righteous man availeth much.

entries.name: Hezekiah spreads out the letter
entries.epithet: Spread it before the LORD
entries.occasion: A threatening letter from the king of Assyria

lines: And Hezekiah prayed before the LORD, and said, O LORD God of Israel, which dwellest between the cherubims, thou art the God, even thou alone, of all the kingdoms of the earth: thou hast made heaven and earth.
LORD, bow down thine ear, and hear: open, LORD, thine eyes, and see: and hear the words of Sennacherib, which hath sent him to reproach the living God.

entries.summary: When the Assyrian king sent a letter mocking God, Hezekiah took it to the temple, spread it out before the LORD, and prayed.
entries.story: Sennacherib's envoy boasted that no god had saved any nation from Assyria. 'And Hezekiah received the letter of the hand of the messengers, and read it: and Hezekiah went up into the house of the LORD, and spread it before the LORD.' He prayed that God would see and hear and save, 'that all the kingdoms of the earth may know that thou art the LORD God, even thou only.' That night the Assyrian army was struck down.
entries.meaning: Hezekiah did not panic or bargain; he laid the problem out before God, quite literally. His prayer, like Elijah's and Solomon's, asked for God's name to be known.
entries.daily: Take the thing that frightens you, a letter, a bill, a diagnosis, and lay it before God. Tell him what it says, and ask him to act.
entries.pray_it: Lord, here is what is troubling me. I lay it out before you. See it, hear it, and act, so that your name is honoured.

key_verses.text: Now therefore, O LORD our God, I beseech thee, save thou us out of his hand, that all the kingdoms of the earth may know that thou art the LORD God, even thou only.

entries.name: The prayer of Jabez
entries.epithet: Oh that thou wouldest bless me indeed
entries.occasion: A prayer remembered in a list of names

lines: And Jabez called on the God of Israel, saying, Oh that thou wouldest bless me indeed, and enlarge my coast, and that thine hand might be with me, and that thou wouldest keep me from evil, that it may not grieve me! And God granted him that which he requested.

entries.summary: In the middle of a list of names, one man is remembered for a single prayer: that God would bless him, be with him and keep him from harm.
entries.story: Jabez's mother named him for the pain of his birth: 'Because I bare him with sorrow.' Yet he 'was more honourable than his brethren', and he 'called on the God of Israel', asking God to bless him, enlarge his borders, keep his hand with him and keep him from evil. 'And God granted him that which he requested.'
entries.meaning: Jabez's prayer is short and personal, asking for God's blessing, his hand and his protection. It shows that God hears ordinary requests, and that a name given in sorrow need not define a life.
entries.daily: It is right to ask God to bless you, to be with you and to keep you from harm. Ask for his hand, not only for his gifts.
entries.pray_it: God, bless me, widen my life for your purposes, keep your hand on me, and keep me from harm.

entries.name: Jehoshaphat: our eyes are upon thee
entries.epithet: Neither know we what to do
entries.occasion: An army far bigger than his own was marching on Judah

lines: O our God, wilt thou not judge them? for we have no might against this great company that cometh against us; neither know we what to do: but our eyes are upon thee.

entries.summary: Facing an invading army far larger than his own, King Jehoshaphat prayed before all Judah: we do not know what to do, but our eyes are on you.
entries.story: A great army from Moab, Ammon and mount Seir was coming against Judah. Jehoshaphat was afraid, 'and set himself to seek the LORD, and proclaimed a fast throughout all Judah.' In the temple court, with all Judah standing 'with their little ones, their wives, and their children', he prayed: 'we have no might against this great company … neither know we what to do: but our eyes are upon thee.' God answered through a Levite: 'the battle is not yours'.
entries.meaning: Admitting helplessness is not a failure of faith; it is where faith begins. The whole community prayed together, children included.
entries.daily: When you do not know what to do, say so to God, and fix your eyes on him instead of on the size of the problem.
entries.pray_it: Lord, I do not know what to do, but my eyes are on you.

entries.name: Daniel's open window
entries.epithet: He kneeled upon his knees three times a day
entries.occasion: When prayer to anyone but the king was made a crime
entries.summary: When praying to anyone but the king was made a crime, Daniel went home and prayed three times a day, as he always had, with his windows open toward Jerusalem.
entries.story: Jealous officials persuaded King Darius to sign a decree that anyone who prayed to any god or man except the king for thirty days would be thrown to the lions. 'Now when Daniel knew that the writing was signed, he went into his house; and his windows being open in his chamber toward Jerusalem, he kneeled upon his knees three times a day, and prayed, and gave thanks before his God, as he did aforetime.' He was thrown to the lions, and God shut their mouths.
entries.meaning: Daniel's courage in the crisis grew out of a habit formed long before. He did not start praying because of the danger; he simply did not stop.
entries.daily: Build a steady rhythm of prayer: morning, midday and evening, or whatever fits your day. Habits formed in calm times hold in hard ones.
entries.pray_it: Lord, as I do every day, I come to you and give you thanks. Keep me faithful, whatever this day brings.

key_verses.text: Now when Daniel knew that the writing was signed, he went into his house; and his windows being open in his chamber toward Jerusalem, he kneeled upon his knees three times a day, and prayed, and gave thanks before his God, as he did aforetime.
Evening, and morning, and at noon, will I pray, and cry aloud: and he shall hear my voice.

entries.name: Daniel's prayer of confession
entries.epithet: O Lord, hear; O Lord, forgive
entries.occasion: Reading Jeremiah's prophecy of seventy years

lines: O my God, incline thine ear, and hear; open thine eyes, and behold our desolations, and the city which is called by thy name: for we do not present our supplications before thee for our righteousnesses, but for thy great mercies.
O Lord, hear; O Lord, forgive; O Lord, hearken and do; defer not, for thine own sake, O my God: for thy city and thy people are called by thy name.

entries.summary: Reading Jeremiah's prophecy of seventy years, Daniel fasted and confessed his people's sins as his own, and pleaded for God's mercy on Jerusalem.
entries.story: In the first year of Darius, Daniel 'understood by books' that Jerusalem would lie desolate for seventy years, as Jeremiah had said. He set his face 'to seek by prayer and supplications, with fasting, and sackcloth, and ashes.' He confessed, 'We have sinned, and have committed iniquity', never excusing himself. He asked for mercy not because of Israel's goodness, 'but for thy great mercies.' While he was still praying, the angel Gabriel came to him.
entries.meaning: Daniel prayed God's promises back to him, and he stood with his people in their sin rather than above them. Confession and hope belong together.
entries.daily: When you pray for your church, family or nation, say 'we', not 'they'. Rest your request on God's mercy, not on anyone's goodness.
entries.pray_it: Lord, we have sinned and gone our own way. We ask not because we deserve it, but because of your great mercy. Hear, forgive and act.

key_verses.text: Then shall ye call upon me, and ye shall go and pray unto me, and I will hearken unto you. And ye shall seek me, and find me, when ye shall search for me with all your heart.

entries.name: Nehemiah's prayer for Jerusalem
entries.epithet: The great and terrible God, that keepeth covenant and mercy
entries.occasion: News that Jerusalem's walls were broken down

lines: And said, I beseech thee, O LORD God of heaven, the great and terrible God, that keepeth covenant and mercy for them that love him and observe his commandments:

entries.summary: Hearing that Jerusalem's walls lay in ruins, Nehemiah wept, fasted and prayed for days, confessing sin and asking God to remember his promise.
entries.story: When Nehemiah heard about Jerusalem's broken walls, he 'sat down and wept, and mourned certain days, and fasted, and prayed before the God of heaven.' He praised God as the one 'that keepeth covenant and mercy for them that love him', confessed Israel's sin including his own, reminded God of his promise to gather the scattered, and asked for success when he went before the king.
entries.meaning: Nehemiah prayed for about four months before he acted (compare the months in Nehemiah 1:1 and 2:1). His plan grew out of prayer, and his prayer was full of God's own words.
entries.daily: Let a burden drive you to prayer before it drives you to action. Pray God's promises back to him, and ask for help with the next practical step.
entries.pray_it: Great and faithful God, this burden is heavy on my heart. Remember your promises, and give me favour and wisdom for what I must do next.

key_verses.text: And it came to pass, when I heard these words, that I sat down and wept, and mourned certain days, and fasted, and prayed before the God of heaven,

entries.name: Nehemiah's prayer in a moment
entries.epithet: So I prayed to the God of heaven
entries.occasion: When the king suddenly asked what he wanted
entries.summary: When the king suddenly asked him what he wanted, Nehemiah sent up a silent prayer to God before he answered.
entries.story: Nehemiah was serving wine to King Artaxerxes when the king noticed his sad face. 'Then I was very sore afraid.' The king asked, 'For what dost thou make request?' And in that moment, between the question and the answer: 'So I prayed to the God of heaven.' Then he asked to be sent to rebuild Jerusalem, and the king agreed, 'according to the good hand of my God upon me.'
entries.meaning: Some prayers take seconds. Nehemiah's silent prayer before the king rested on months of prayer before it.
entries.daily: Pray in the moment: before you answer a hard question, walk into a meeting or pick up the phone. A breath and a silent “Lord, help” is real prayer.
entries.pray_it: Lord, help me now. Give me the right words.

key_verses.text: Then the king said unto me, For what dost thou make request? So I prayed to the God of heaven.

entries.name: Jeremiah: nothing too hard
entries.epithet: There is nothing too hard for thee
entries.occasion: Buying a field while Jerusalem was under siege
entries.where: The court of the prison in Jerusalem

lines: Ah Lord GOD! behold, thou hast made the heaven and the earth by thy great power and stretched out arm, and there is nothing too hard for thee:

entries.summary: With Jerusalem under siege, Jeremiah bought a field as God told him to, and then prayed, confessing that nothing is too hard for God.
entries.story: Babylon's army surrounded Jerusalem, and Jeremiah was in prison. God told him to buy his cousin's field at Anathoth, as a sign that 'Houses and fields and vineyards shall be possessed again in this land.' Jeremiah obeyed, and then prayed: 'Ah Lord GOD! behold, thou hast made the heaven and the earth by thy great power … there is nothing too hard for thee.' God answered with his own question: 'Behold, I am the LORD, the God of all flesh: is there any thing too hard for me?'
entries.meaning: Jeremiah obeyed first, and prayed through his questions afterwards. His prayer starts with creation: the God who made everything can keep his promises.
entries.daily: When one of God's promises seems impossible in your situation, begin your prayer where Jeremiah did: with what God has already done.
entries.pray_it: Lord God, you made the heavens and the earth. Nothing is too hard for you, not even this.

key_verses.text: Behold, I am the LORD, the God of all flesh: is there any thing too hard for me?
Call unto me, and I will answer thee, and shew thee great and mighty things, which thou knowest not.

entries.name: A morning prayer
entries.epithet: In the morning will I direct my prayer unto thee
entries.occasion: The start of the day

lines: Give ear to my words, O LORD, consider my meditation.
Hearken unto the voice of my cry, my King, and my God: for unto thee will I pray.
My voice shalt thou hear in the morning, O LORD; in the morning will I direct my prayer unto thee, and will look up.

entries.summary: A prayer for the start of the day: to lay your words before God in the morning, and then to watch for his answer.
entries.story: Psalm 5 is headed as a psalm of David. It begins, 'Give ear to my words, O LORD, consider my meditation.' Then it makes a promise about the start of each day: 'in the morning will I direct my prayer unto thee, and will look up.' The rest of the psalm asks God to lead him in righteousness among his enemies, and ends in joy for all who trust in God.
entries.meaning: The Hebrew word behind 'direct' is used for setting things out in order, like an offering on an altar. David laid his requests before God in the morning, and then kept looking up for the answer through the day.
entries.daily: Begin the day by laying your plans and concerns before God, then look up to him through the day for his answers.
entries.pray_it: Lord, hear my voice this morning. I lay this day before you. Lead me, and help me look up to you all day long.

key_verses.text: But let all those that put their trust in thee rejoice: let them ever shout for joy, because thou defendest them: let them also that love thy name be joyful in thee.

entries.name: An evening prayer
entries.epithet: I will both lay me down in peace, and sleep
entries.occasion: The end of the day

lines: There be many that say, Who will shew us any good? LORD, lift thou up the light of thy countenance upon us.
Thou hast put gladness in my heart, more than in the time that their corn and their wine increased.

entries.summary: A prayer for the end of the day: trust that lets you lie down and sleep in peace, because God keeps you safe.
entries.story: Psalm 4 is David's cry to God in trouble: 'Hear me when I call, O God of my righteousness.' He tells others to 'commune with your own heart upon your bed, and be still.' It ends with the psalmist lying down for the night: 'I will both lay me down in peace, and sleep: for thou, LORD, only makest me dwell in safety.'
entries.meaning: Sleep is an act of trust. Worries do not have to be solved before bedtime; they can be handed to the God who keeps watch.
entries.daily: Before you sleep, hand the day's unfinished business to God, and then rest.
entries.pray_it: Lord, I lay down the worries of today. You alone keep me safe. I will lie down in peace and sleep.

key_verses.text: I laid me down and slept; I awaked; for the LORD sustained me.

entries.name: A prayer of confession
entries.epithet: Have mercy upon me, O God
entries.occasion: After Nathan confronted him over Bathsheba

lines: Have mercy upon me, O God, according to thy lovingkindness: according unto the multitude of thy tender mercies blot out my transgressions.
Wash me throughly from mine iniquity, and cleanse me from my sin.
Create in me a clean heart, O God; and renew a right spirit within me.

entries.summary: David's prayer of repentance after Nathan confronted him, asking not only to be pardoned but to be given a clean heart.
entries.story: After David took Bathsheba and had Uriah killed, the prophet Nathan confronted him. Psalm 51 is headed as David's prayer from that time. It begins with God's mercy: 'Have mercy upon me, O God, according to thy lovingkindness.' It hides nothing: 'my sin is ever before me.' And it asks for a new start: 'Create in me a clean heart, O God; and renew a right spirit within me.'
entries.meaning: Confession is not only admitting wrong, but asking God to change us. 'A broken and a contrite heart, O God, thou wilt not despise' (Psalm 51:17).
entries.daily: Confess sin specifically and soon, and ask not only to be forgiven but to be made new.
entries.pray_it: God, have mercy on me. Wash me clean, create a clean heart in me, and give me back the joy of your salvation.

key_verses.text: The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit: a broken and a contrite heart, O God, thou wilt not despise.
If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins, and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.

entries.name: A prayer for guidance
entries.epithet: Shew me thy ways, O LORD
entries.occasion: Needing direction

lines: Shew me thy ways, O LORD; teach me thy paths.
Lead me in thy truth, and teach me: for thou art the God of my salvation; on thee do I wait all the day.

entries.summary: A prayer for guidance, asking God to show, to teach and to lead, and a promise to wait on him all day.
entries.story: Psalm 25 is an acrostic: each verse begins with the next letter of the Hebrew alphabet. In it David asks not to be put to shame, remembers the sins of his youth, and prays: 'Shew me thy ways, O LORD; teach me thy paths. Lead me in thy truth, and teach me: for thou art the God of my salvation; on thee do I wait all the day.'
entries.meaning: Guidance in the Bible is less about getting a single answer and more about learning God's ways over a lifetime, waiting on him 'all the day'.
entries.daily: Before you plan the day, ask God to show you his way through it, and keep listening as you go.
entries.pray_it: Lord, show me your ways and teach me your paths. Lead me in your truth today; I am waiting on you.

key_verses.text: The meek will he guide in judgment: and the meek will he teach his way.

entries.name: A prayer from the cave
entries.epithet: I poured out my complaint before him
entries.occasion: Hiding from Saul, alone

lines: I cried unto the LORD with my voice; with my voice unto the LORD did I make my supplication.
I poured out my complaint before him; I shewed before him my trouble.

entries.summary: A prayer of David when he hid in a cave, alone and hunted: he pours out his complaint to God and finds him to be his refuge.
entries.story: The psalm is headed “A Prayer when he was in the cave”, from the years David hid from Saul. 'I cried unto the LORD with my voice … I poured out my complaint before him; I shewed before him my trouble.' He looked around, and 'no man cared for my soul.' Yet he said to God, 'Thou art my refuge and my portion in the land of the living.'
entries.meaning: The Bible does not ask us to hide our complaints from God, but to bring them to him. David's lament turns to trust without pretending the cave was not dark.
entries.daily: Loneliness and pressure can become prayer. Tell God exactly what is wrong; he is a refuge when no one else seems to care.
entries.pray_it: Lord, I pour out my trouble to you. I feel alone, but you are my refuge and my portion. Bring me out of this place.

key_verses.text: I cried unto thee, O LORD: I said, Thou art my refuge and my portion in the land of the living.

entries.name: Search me, O God
entries.epithet: Search me, O God, and know my heart
entries.occasion: Wonder at how fully God knows us

lines: Search me, O God, and know my heart: try me, and know my thoughts:

entries.summary: A prayer asking God to search the heart and lead in the way everlasting, from a psalm about how fully God knows us.
entries.story: Psalm 139 marvels that God knows us completely: when we sit down and when we get up, our thoughts from far away, every word before it is spoken. There is nowhere to flee from his presence, and he formed us in the womb. The psalm ends in prayer: 'Search me, O God, and know my heart: try me, and know my thoughts: And see if there be any wicked way in me, and lead me in the way everlasting.'
entries.meaning: Being fully known by God is not a threat but a comfort, and it makes honest self-examination safe. The prayer asks God to find what is wrong, and to lead us on.
entries.daily: At the end of a day, ask God to show you anything that needs to change, and to lead you in his way tomorrow.
entries.pray_it: Search me, God, and know my heart. Show me anything in me that grieves you, and lead me in your everlasting way.

key_verses.text: O LORD, thou hast searched me, and known me. Thou knowest my downsitting and mine uprising, thou understandest my thought afar off.

entries.name: Let the words of my mouth
entries.epithet: Acceptable in thy sight, O LORD
entries.occasion: Before speaking

lines: Who can understand his errors? cleanse thou me from secret faults.
Keep back thy servant also from presumptuous sins; let them not have dominion over me: then shall I be upright, and I shall be innocent from the great transgression.

entries.summary: A prayer for hidden faults to be cleansed, and for our words and thoughts to please God.
entries.story: Psalm 19 praises God's glory in the heavens and the perfection of his law. Then it turns to prayer: 'Who can understand his errors? cleanse thou me from secret faults.' It asks to be kept from presumptuous sins, and ends with a prayer many say before they speak or preach: 'Let the words of my mouth, and the meditation of my heart, be acceptable in thy sight, O LORD, my strength, and my redeemer.'
entries.meaning: The psalm moves from the stars, to God's word, to the words and thoughts of one person. God cares about both what we say and what we think.
entries.daily: Pray this before a conversation, a meeting, or a message you need to write.
entries.pray_it: Lord, my strength and my redeemer, let my words today, and the thoughts behind them, please you.

entries.name: The church prays for boldness
entries.epithet: That with all boldness they may speak thy word
entries.occasion: After Peter and John were threatened by the council

lines: And now, Lord, behold their threatenings: and grant unto thy servants, that with all boldness they may speak thy word,
By stretching forth thine hand to heal; and that signs and wonders may be done by the name of thy holy child Jesus.

entries.summary: When Peter and John were threatened and released, the believers prayed together, not for safety, but for boldness to keep speaking.
entries.story: The council had ordered Peter and John to stop speaking in the name of Jesus. When they were released, the believers 'lifted up their voice to God with one accord.' They began with God as Creator, remembered how the rulers had gathered against Jesus, and asked, 'Lord, behold their threatenings: and grant unto thy servants, that with all boldness they may speak thy word.' The place shook, 'and they were all filled with the Holy Ghost, and they spake the word of God with boldness.'
entries.meaning: The first church prayed for courage rather than comfort, and they began with who God is before they turned to their problem.
entries.daily: When you face opposition, ask for boldness to keep doing what is right, not only for the opposition to go away.
entries.pray_it: Lord, you made heaven and earth, and you see what we face. Give us boldness to speak your word and to live it.

key_verses.text: And when they had prayed, the place was shaken where they were assembled together; and they were all filled with the Holy Ghost, and they spake the word of God with boldness.

entries.name: Stephen's dying prayer
entries.epithet: Lord Jesus, receive my spirit
entries.occasion: As he was stoned

lines: And they stoned Stephen, calling upon God, and saying, Lord Jesus, receive my spirit.
And he kneeled down, and cried with a loud voice, Lord, lay not this sin to their charge. And when he had said this, he fell asleep.

entries.summary: As he was stoned, Stephen entrusted his spirit to Jesus and prayed for his killers to be forgiven.
entries.story: Stephen saw heaven opened and Jesus standing at the right hand of God. The council rushed on him, dragged him out of the city and stoned him, while he was 'calling upon God, and saying, Lord Jesus, receive my spirit. And he kneeled down, and cried with a loud voice, Lord, lay not this sin to their charge. And when he had said this, he fell asleep.'
entries.meaning: Stephen's two prayers echo Jesus' two prayers from the cross (Luke 23:34, 46). He had learned to pray like his Lord, even in death.
entries.daily: Let Jesus' prayers become yours: trust for yourself, and forgiveness for others.
entries.pray_it: Lord Jesus, I trust myself to you. Do not hold against others the wrong they have done to me.

entries.name: Paul's prayer for the Ephesians
entries.epithet: The love of Christ, which passeth knowledge
entries.occasion: A letter from prison to the church at Ephesus

lines: That Christ may dwell in your hearts by faith; that ye, being rooted and grounded in love,
May be able to comprehend with all saints what is the breadth, and length, and depth, and height;
And to know the love of Christ, which passeth knowledge, that ye might be filled with all the fulness of God.
Now unto him that is able to do exceeding abundantly above all that we ask or think, according to the power that worketh in us,
Unto him be glory in the church by Christ Jesus throughout all ages, world without end. Amen.

entries.summary: Paul knelt and prayed that believers would be strengthened by the Spirit, know Christ's love beyond knowing, and be filled with God's fulness.
entries.story: Writing from prison, Paul said, 'For this cause I bow my knees unto the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ.' He prayed for inner strength by the Spirit, for Christ to dwell in their hearts by faith, and that they would grasp the breadth, length, depth and height of his love. He ended in praise 'unto him that is able to do exceeding abundantly above all that we ask or think.'
entries.meaning: Paul's prayers for others ask for inner, spiritual gifts: strength, faith, love and the knowledge of God, more than for easier circumstances.
entries.daily: Pray for the people you love the way Paul did: that they would know how much Christ loves them.
entries.pray_it: Father, strengthen the people I love by your Spirit. Let Christ live in their hearts, and let them know how wide and deep his love is.

key_verses.text: That he would grant you, according to the riches of his glory, to be strengthened with might by his Spirit in the inner man;

entries.name: Paul's prayer for the Philippians
entries.epithet: That your love may abound yet more and more
entries.occasion: A letter of thanks to the church at Philippi

lines: And this I pray, that your love may abound yet more and more in knowledge and in all judgment;
That ye may approve things that are excellent; that ye may be sincere and without offence till the day of Christ;
Being filled with the fruits of righteousness, which are by Jesus Christ, unto the glory and praise of God.

entries.summary: Paul thanked God with joy for the believers at Philippi, and prayed that their love would grow in knowledge and wisdom.
entries.story: Paul wrote, 'I thank my God upon every remembrance of you, Always in every prayer of mine for you all making request with joy.' He was sure that God, who had begun a good work in them, would finish it. He prayed 'that your love may abound yet more and more in knowledge and in all judgment', so that they would approve what is excellent and be filled with the fruits of righteousness.
entries.meaning: Thanksgiving comes first in Paul's prayers. And he prays not only that love will grow, but that it will grow wise.
entries.daily: Thank God for particular people before you pray for their needs, and pray that their love, and yours, grows wiser.
entries.pray_it: Thank you, God, for the people you have given me. Make our love grow, full of wisdom and good sense, until the day of Christ.

key_verses.text: Being confident of this very thing, that he which hath begun a good work in you will perform it until the day of Jesus Christ:

entries.name: Be careful for nothing
entries.epithet: The peace of God, which passeth all understanding
entries.occasion: Teaching on worry, written from prison

lines: Be careful for nothing; but in every thing by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving let your requests be made known unto God.
And the peace of God, which passeth all understanding, shall keep your hearts and minds through Christ Jesus.

entries.summary: Paul's teaching on anxiety: instead of worrying about anything, pray about everything with thanksgiving, and God's peace will guard your heart.
entries.story: Paul wrote this from prison, facing a trial that could end in his death. 'Be careful for nothing; but in every thing by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving let your requests be made known unto God. And the peace of God, which passeth all understanding, shall keep your hearts and minds through Christ Jesus.' In the English of 1611, “careful” means full of care: anxious.
entries.meaning: Paul does not promise that every request will be granted, but that God's peace will stand guard over our hearts. Thanksgiving is part of the cure for worry.
entries.daily: Turn each worry into a request as it comes, add something to thank God for, and leave it with him.
entries.pray_it: Lord, this is what I am anxious about. I give it to you, with thanks for all you have done, and I ask for your peace.

key_verses.text: Casting all your care upon him; for he careth for you.

entries.name: Pray without ceasing
entries.epithet: In every thing give thanks
entries.occasion: Closing words to the church at Thessalonica

lines: Rejoice evermore.
Pray without ceasing.
In every thing give thanks: for this is the will of God in Christ Jesus concerning you.

entries.summary: Three short commands for daily life: rejoice always, pray without ceasing, and give thanks in everything.
entries.story: At the end of his first letter to the Thessalonians, Paul gave a run of short instructions. Three of them belong together: 'Rejoice evermore. Pray without ceasing. In every thing give thanks: for this is the will of God in Christ Jesus concerning you.'
entries.meaning: Praying without ceasing does not mean saying words every minute, but living the whole day in conversation with God. It is one of the Bible's plainest statements of God's will for ordinary life.
entries.daily: Turn ordinary moments into prayer: a line of thanks while you wait, a request as you walk, a word of praise when something goes well.
entries.pray_it: Lord, be with me in every moment today. I will talk with you as I go, and thank you for everything.

entries.name: The prayer of faith
entries.epithet: The effectual fervent prayer of a righteous man availeth much
entries.occasion: Closing words of his letter

lines: Confess your faults one to another, and pray one for another, that ye may be healed. The effectual fervent prayer of a righteous man availeth much.

entries.summary: James urges prayer in every situation: when suffering, when happy, when sick, and when we have sinned, and points to Elijah as an example.
entries.story: 'Is any among you afflicted? let him pray. Is any merry? let him sing psalms.' The sick are to call for the elders of the church to pray over them. 'Confess your faults one to another, and pray one for another, that ye may be healed.' Then James reminds his readers that Elijah 'was a man subject to like passions as we are', and his prayers shut and opened the heavens.
entries.meaning: Prayer is for every mood and every need, and it is meant to be shared: confessing to one another and praying for one another.
entries.daily: Match your prayer to your day: ask when it is hard, praise when it is good, and ask a friend to pray with you when you are struggling.
entries.pray_it: Lord, you heard the prayers of an ordinary man like Elijah. Hear my prayers today, and use me to pray for others.

key_verses.text: Is any among you afflicted? let him pray. Is any merry? let him sing psalms.

entries.name: Even so, come, Lord Jesus
entries.epithet: The last prayer in the Bible
entries.occasion: The close of Revelation

lines: He which testifieth these things saith, Surely I come quickly. Amen. Even so, come, Lord Jesus.

entries.summary: The last prayer in the Bible: when the risen Jesus says 'Surely I come quickly', John answers, 'Amen. Even so, come, Lord Jesus.'
entries.story: Revelation ends with Jesus' promise and John's reply: 'He which testifieth these things saith, Surely I come quickly. Amen. Even so, come, Lord Jesus.' The first Christians had a short Aramaic prayer usually understood to mean the same, Maranatha, “Our Lord, come” (1 Corinthians 16:22).
entries.meaning: Christian prayer looks forward. The Bible's final prayer asks for Jesus himself to come, and to make all things new.
entries.daily: Let the hope of Christ's return shape your prayers, especially on hard days. The last word is his coming.
entries.pray_it: Come, Lord Jesus. Until you do, keep me faithful and full of hope.
